source_text: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research, 28 August 2026. Hyperscaler capex: raising our 2026 estimate to $751B. We now expect 2026 hyperscaler capex of $751B, up from $671B two weeks ago, after Microsoft and Meta guided above consensus. The driver is not demand for inference alone: the four largest buyers are pulling forward 2027 orders to secure HBM and CoWoS capacity, which is sold out through the first half of 2027. That supply lock is why we think the cycle extends rather than peaks: as long as memory pricing keeps rising (we model +18% for HBM contract prices into 1Q27), the capex guides keep rising with it, because the constraint is supply, not appetite. We remain Buy on NVDA with a $250 price target. The risk to the view is a memory price rollover: if HBM contract prices fall for two consecutive months, the pull-forward argument breaks and 2027 capex guides would be cut. We do not expect a Fed rate decision to change this picture.

sentences_source_text: J.P. Morgan Rates Strategy, 31 August 2026. The 10-year yield broke 4.40% on Friday for the first time since May. We think the move is a bear-steepener: the front end is anchored by a Fed on hold, so the long end is doing the work as term premium rebuilds. We recommend paying 5s30s at 62bp with a stop at 48bp. Citi's rates desk, by contrast, sees the break as a positioning flush and expects 4.40% to hold on a closing basis. A hot core PCE print on Thursday (consensus 0.3% m/m) would validate our steepener; a soft print would not by itself reverse it while the Fed stays on hold.
